glosses: A clumsy or embarrassing mistake.
A very bad move, usually caused by some tactical oversight.
Confusion; bewilderment; trouble; disturbance; clamour.
To make a big mistake, especially when it is careless or stupid.

examples.text: to blunder in preparing a medical prescription

glosses: To make a big mistake, especially when it is careless or stupid.
To make a bad move, especially caused by tactical oversight.
To make a big mistake, especially when it is careless or stupid.
To lose a piece due to having made a bad move [with the piece lost].

examples.text: blunder a rook

glosses: To make a big mistake, especially when it is careless or stupid.
To overlook the possibility of, or end up in, a specified undesirable situation after making a bad move.

examples.text: blunder a draw
blunder a mate in one

glosses: To move in an unsteady way.

examples.text: I was never distinguished for address, and have often even blundered in making my bow.
blunders on, and staggers every pace

glosses: To enter a place or become involved in a difficult situation by mistake.

examples.text: He and I had blundered into the middle of a gang fight once and I saw him shank a guy-stuck homeboy in the chest and strolled off cool as you please.

glosses: To do or treat in a blundering manner; to confuse.

examples.text: He blunders and confounds all these together.

Were a Diſpute to be manag'd purely for a Trial of Skill; then to ſhuffle and digreſs from the Matter in hand, ſo as by any means whatſoever to blunder an Adverſary, and ſtop the Progreſs of his Argument, were a more pardonable Piece of Folly.
